raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Adds a CUDA kernel, `gelu_tanh_and_mul_per_token_quant`, and the `(GeluAndMul, per-token dynamic FP8)` row in the manual activation+quant fusion registry, as part of the manual fusion port (#43501, #43224). When GELU runs as the CUDA `gelu_and_mul` op, Gemma3 and Gemma 4 FP8-dynamic MLPs produce the down projection's input in one kernel instead of `gelu_tanh_and_mul` followed by `dynamic_per_token_scaled_fp8_quant`.

## Claims

- Output is unchanged: byte-identical to the two kernels it replaces on every call of real Gemma3 and Gemma 4 generations, on L4, H100 and B200.
- On the CUDA-op path, MLP activation+quant is 1.41-1.79× faster. On Gemma-4-31B (H100) it is 1.47× faster than main and 1.36× faster than the compiled kernel.
- bs32 latency improves 1.46% on Gemma-4-31B (H100), and 3.35% (L4), 1.63% (H100) and 2.71% (B200) on Gemma3-1B.
- The `torch.compile` default path is unchanged. The row only replaces the CUDA `gelu_and_mul` op.

## Validation

CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14, bf16, `--kernel-config.linear_backend=cutlass`, `RedHatAI/gemma-*-it-FP8-dynamic`.

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_quant_activation.py                    # 173 passed
pytest tests/compile/passes/test_silu_mul_quant_manual_fusion.py       # 38 passed, 12 skipped (50 passed on B200)
pytest tests/quantization/test_compressed_tensors.py -k gemma3_dynamic_fp8_gelu_fusion  # 2 passed
pytest tests/compile/passes/test_functionalization.py                  # 14 passed
```

H100 ran these on this commit's base, `5d55ef1590`. Generation also passes with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, with CUDA custom ops and with `--enforce-eager`, on Gemma3-1B and Gemma-4-31B.

**Exactness.** During a real generation (128 gsm8k prompts × 128 tokens), every call also ran the two original kernels on the same input, and FP8 values and scales were compared byte for byte:

| GPU | model | calls | token rows | differences |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L4 | Gemma3-1B | 3,380 | 852,228 | 0 |
| L4 | Gemma3-4B | 4,420 | 1,140,054 | 0 |
| H100 | Gemma3-1B | 3,380 | 1,494,220 | 0 |
| B200 | Gemma3-1B | 3,432 | 1,501,396 | 0 |
| H100 | Gemma-4-31B | 7,800 | 3,478,740 | 0 |

On Gemma-4-31B, greedy token IDs also match with and without the row on 5 prompts (H100, CUDA ops).

**End to end**, CUDA ops, main → this PR, mean of 2 runs in main-PR-PR-main order:

| GPU, model | bs1 latency (s) | bs32 latency (s) | throughput (tok/s) | compiled default (bs1 / bs32 / tok/s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L4, Gemma3-1B | 0.9721 → 0.9653 (+0.70%) | 2.4744 → 2.3915 (+3.35%) | 12853 → 13231 (+2.94%) | 0.9628 / 2.3807 / 13300 |
| L4, Gemma3-4B | 2.8926 → 2.8881 (+0.16%) | 9.0574 → 8.9037 (+1.70%) | 3499 → 3558 (+1.71%) | 2.8808 / 8.8920 / 3569 |
| H100, Gemma3-1B | 0.2839 → 0.2776 (+2.20%) | 0.4207 → 0.4139 (+1.63%) | 97945 → 99990 (+2.09%) | 0.2601 / 0.3887 / 98275 |
| B200, Gemma3-1B | 0.2418 → 0.2372 (+1.92%) | 0.3241 → 0.3153 (+2.71%) | 142050 → 146751 (+3.31%) | 0.2200 / 0.2966 / 152154 |
| H100, Gemma-4-31B | not run | 5.7351 → 5.6516 (+1.46%) | not resolved | not run |

Throughput varies 2.6-3% between runs of one setup on H100 and up to 7% on B200, so I don't count those H100 and B200 cells as gains. The Gemma-4-31B run hit its time limit before the compiled arm and the last main throughput run.

**GPU time**, `torch.profiler`, 32 prompts × 1024 in / 128 out, ms:

| GPU, model | MLP act+quant, main → PR | same step, compiled | total, main → PR | total, compiled |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L4, Gemma3-1B | 245.8 → 137.4 | 137.9 | 2426.6 → 2334.7 (−3.79%) | 2316.0 |
| H100, Gemma3-1B | about 36.6 → 24.7 | 25.9 | 385.7 → 374.2 (−2.99%) | 356.9 |
| B200, Gemma3-1B | about 34.8 → 24.6 | 24.7 | 314.0 → 304.4 (−3.07%) | 281.6 |
| H100, Gemma-4-31B | about 275.9 → 188.1 | 255.0 | 5652.2 → 5571.3 (−1.43%) | 5578.9 |

<details>
<summary>Kernel benchmark and gsm8k</summary>

```bash
python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_activation.py --func-name gelu_and_mul_tanh --quantize-fp8
```

L4, µs, median of `triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph`, bf16, the two kernels → this kernel. All 20 shapes are 1.12-3.2× faster, and fp16 is within 2%.

| width (Gemma3) | 1 token | 16 | 128 | 512 | 2048 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6912 (1B) | 4.87 → 3.27 | 4.98 → 3.33 | 9.29 → 7.12 | 26.1 → 23.2 | 424 → 281 |
| 10240 (4B) | 6.23 → 4.25 | 6.38 → 4.36 | 12.6 → 9.93 | 43.5 → 33.4 | 739 → 410 |
| 15360 (12B) | 7.56 → 5.20 | 7.73 → 5.26 | 16.7 → 13.4 | 171 → 53.2 | 1165 → 613 |
| 21504 (27B) | 9.71 → 6.73 | 10.1 → 6.79 | 23.1 → 20.3 | 292 → 163 | 1639 → 859 |

Standalone comparison at the same widths and 1-8192 tokens, L2-warm / flushed: H100 1.22-1.72× / 1.28-1.72×, B200 1.08-1.54× / 1.11-1.50×, faster on 24/24 shapes on both. Random inputs are bit-exact on 72/72 cases on both (bf16 and fp16, with and without `scale_ub`).

gsm8k, greedy, 1319 questions, CUDA ops, L4. End-to-end runs are not deterministic on main, and these stay within its spread:

| run | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 4B, offline | 0.7672, 0.7627 | 0.7604 |
| 4B, server | 0.763 | 0.754 |
| 1B, server | 0.267 | 0.262 |

</details>

Benchmarks and exactness ran on older trees with this same kernel file: `e96b490b12` (H100, Gemma3) and `e0d00e4b8e` (B200, and H100 Gemma-4-31B).

## Details

- **Design.** One thread block per token: compute the row and its absmax, then quantize with `scaled_fp8_conversion`, from shared memory when the row fits. The GELU expression and rounding are copied from `gelu_tanh_kernel` and `act_and_mul_kernel`, which is what keeps the output identical.
- **Default path.** Under `torch.compile`, Inductor fuses GELU with the quantization using its own FP8 rounding, so the row skips that path and output stays unchanged.
- **Limits.** On Gemma3-1B this path stays behind compiled latency, about 6.5% on H100 and 6-8% on B200, against 0.5% at bs32 on an L4. The other per-token quant calls are the largest remaining piece (64.1 ms on H100, 68.4 ms on B200), and this PR does not touch them. On Gemma-4-31B, total GPU time is level with compiled, but I have no compiled latency. The block size was chosen on the L4: it averages 0.9% / 1.6% (H100) and 0.8% / 1.4% (B200) warm / flushed from the best, worst 14% / 21% and 11% / 17% at d=6912, 256 tokens. 4B end to end and gsm8k were not run on H100 or B200.
- **Scope.** Dense `Gemma3MLP` and `Gemma4MLP`. Gemma 4 MoE layers fuse the activation in their expert kernels. `Gemma4Unified` is not checked.
- **CI.** The Quantization job is disabled (#63608), so the Gemma3 test runs in the H100 Fusion E2E Quick job. Gemma-4-31B is validated outside CI.
- **Related.** #58664 (SiLU per-token), #59467 (NVFP4 GELU) and #64854 (static FP8 GELU) do not add this row. #59467 adds the same `gemma3.py` line, and #59467 and #64854 add the same `gemma4.py` line. I can merge this kernel with #58664's into one activation-templated kernel as a follow-up.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [ ] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
